feedback.problem:
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{4}^{32}\frac{1}{x\sqrt{{log}_{2}⁡x}}\,\text{d}x=($
{{field-1}}
$)\operatorname{ln}⁡2$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{2}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot \text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $4$ | $32$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $2$ | $5$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{4}^{32}\frac{1}{x\sqrt{{log}_{2}⁡x}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{4}^{32}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{log}_{2}⁡x}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{5}\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2{\int }_{2}^{5}\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot 2\sqrt{u}\,{|}_{2}^{5} \\  & =(2\sqrt{5}-2\sqrt{2})\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$
